title: Shingles vaccine
what: A vaccine shot that lowers the risk of shingles and the severe pain that can follow. Usually 2 shots are given.
why: For people over 50 and adults with weakened immunity, as advised by a doctor.
duration: the shot takes a few seconds; with the check-up usually 15 to 40 minutes; the second shot is usually 2 to 6 months later
tell_doctor: If you are sick now or have a fever
Allergies and strong reactions to past vaccines
If you receive treatment that lowers immunity

prepare.title: Health
prepare.text: The vaccine is given when you are healthy. You will be examined before the shot.

prepare.title: Schedule
prepare.text: The course is usually 2 shots. Write down the date of the second.

prepare.title: After the shot
prepare.text: Many people feel weak for 1 to 2 days. It is better not to plan important things for the next day.

steps: A doctor or nurse asks how you feel and takes your temperature
The skin is wiped and the shot is given
The vaccine is recorded in the documents
After the shot, sit at the clinic for about 30 minutes
feel: Often the spot aches and turns red for 1 to 3 days
Sometimes weakness, body aches, chills or fever. It passes on its own
after: Stay near the office for 30 minutes
You can go back to your usual activities
Do not forget the second shot
red_flags: Trouble breathing, swelling of the face or throat, a rash all over: call your local emergency number

faq.q: Do I need the vaccine if I already had shingles?
faq.a: Often yes, shingles can come back. The doctor will say when to get it.

faq.q: Do I need it if I had chickenpox?
faq.a: Yes. Shingles is caused by the same virus as chickenpox.

reminders.text: Shingles vaccine tomorrow. Bring your vaccination record.
